htf_bias: Bearish - higher high rejected, closing at the low

ssl.label: TP1 - median next-day low excursion for this setup

narrative: CALLED AT ~15:05 IST, 25 MINUTES BEFORE THE BELL, AFTER FIVE PRIOR NO_TRADE ANSWERS ON THE SAME QUESTION. Setup: 26-Aug made a higher high than 25-Aug (24378.60 vs 24334.55) and was closing weak, which cuts the measured mean overnight gap from a +15.4 baseline to +2.7 across 343 historical instances. Direction was the real finding; the expression was the problem. STRIKE SELECTION WAS THE PART THAT HELD UP. A scan of every strike within 300 points found the highest expectancy at 24500-24600 PE, but those printed delta -1.000 - synthetic shorts, futures in disguise, outside what this user trades and carrying no optionality at all. The 24400 PE was chosen as the best strike with REAL optionality: delta -0.672, 3.78m OI, 114.5m volume and a 0.13 percent bid/ask spread, the tightest on the board. Solved IV 8.48 percent against the broker's published 5.68 - a -29.34 percent error, the worst seen on this chain, so anyone pricing off the screen was badly wrong about what they were paying. EV WAS STATED AS NEGATIVE AND THE TRADE WON ANYWAY. Modelled expectancy was -76 rupees a lot: the directional edge was real but theta and roughly 130 rupees of round-trip fees consumed it over a one-night hold. NIFTY then fell 78.25 points in the last 25 minutes to close at 24207.75, the low of the day, 16.25 points THROUGH the 24224.00 TP1. The trade paid between +17 and +37 percent depending on how much of the fall the forward passed through - a range, not a number, because the basis pass-through was only ever measured on a RALLY (25-Aug) and its behaviour on a decline is untested. One night is not evidence against a distribution measured over 343 of them: it won on direction, and the negative EV came from costs a same-session exit never paid. THE DEFECT: THE ENTRY WAS LABELLED 'AT THE CLOSE' BUT 24286.00 WAS THE 15:05 PRICE. By the actual 15:30 close spot was 24207.75. Anyone following the instruction literally would have bought the put around 163 instead of 118.70, entering AFTER the move with TP1 already passed and the setup's negative overnight EV fully in front of them. The call was only good if acted on immediately. See [[entry-instructions-need-a-timestamp]]. VERIFIER: 3 of 24 checks fail and all three are LEFT failing on purpose. Check 8 (R:R 0.97 vs the 2.0 floor) is accurate - this was a near target sized to the measured median excursion, not to a ratio. Check 9 is the REAL fault: the 24350.00 stop sits INSIDE the 24350.00-24378.60 rejection block it was meant to protect against, which is the THIRD time in two days the same error was made (25-Aug BTST, 26-Aug fade, this). The stop is deliberately NOT moved retroactively - the call was made at 24350.00 and editing it now would falsify the record. A structurally honest stop above 24378.60 would have been 92.60 points, turning R:R to 0.67.
invalidation: A 5M close above 24350.00 puts price back above the session midpoint and says the late-day weakness was noise rather than distribution. The level sits 64.00 points from entry. NOTE the trade never came close to testing it - the move went straight to target within 25 minutes.
note: NOT TAKEN. The user confirmed after the close that they took NO trades on 26-Aug, and called this one a good call. P&L contribution ZERO. Logged so the CALL is scored - it reached TP1 at 15:25-15:30 on the same session, 16.25 points through target, for a modelled +17 to +37 percent on a 7,699 rupee debit depending on basis pass-through.
